moment_track.max: by length: 4–6 up to 15 min, 8–12 up to 45, 12–18 up to 90, 1 per 6 min beyond
moment_track.chars: label ≤ 60; every moment says what it established

assemblerItemCapsNote: HARD per-component item caps enforced by the assembler (_cap_tab_items in assembly/core.py). Deliberately INDEPENDENT of densityGates above: densityGates is advisory steering text shown to the planner LLM (what to aim for), these caps are the code backstop (what ships regardless of prompt drift) — e.g. step_player is steered to 10 but capped at 25. moment_track's cap follows the video's length strictly (momentCapsByDuration, content-model §9 — Kfir 2026-10-21, no slack): one moment per band step for a label-only track, the band's maximum for a described one, rank-sampled by salience; its density gate (assembly/density.py) refuses a track where most moments say nothing of what they established — the moment fallback chain fills it instead (R7). A key-ideas tab (learning.keyIdeas) is capped instead at keyIdeasCapFactor × keyIdeasByDuration's count for the video's length (Kfir 2026-10-21: extraction stays complete, key ideas are the argument and are never sampled down to a screen — S01 63 min → 24), rank-sampled by richness in source order, above this cap where the video is long.
injectedTabsNote: The tabs assembly adds on its own — the overview hero, the minimum-tab takeaways fallback, the auto-appended frames gallery and the always-present Moments tab (also streamed at plan-done) — with their label, emoji and goal. A goal names what the viewer gets (task 1.10's rule, plan_prompt.goal_rule_violation), never an assembly template; every defaultTab goal (backfills, fillers, the fallback plan) follows the same rule.

momentCapsNote: Moments sized to the video (content-model §9, R9): the first band whose maxMinutes the video's length does not exceed (null = no upper bound) gives one moment per minutesPerMoment, clamped to [min, max]. The last band's floor 18 (the 45–90 band's ceiling, so a longer video never gets fewer moments) and ceiling 60 (a six-hour video) are assembly's choice; learning.timestamps' cap is that 60. A described track (most moments say what they established) ships up to its band's max — for the open-ended last band, whose row states only a rate, one per minutesPerMoment within [min, max] — strictly the table, no slack (Kfir 2026-10-21). Read by assembly/sampling.py.
assemblyPolicyNote: Component and domain sets assembly used to hard-code (output-quality D8 single-sourcing, task 1.8). sequentialComponents: a procedure ships whole and in order — no item cap samples it, the dedupe never trims it, and it is what makes the steps the timeline (D6). stepListDomains: whose steps are followed, not browsed — never promoted to a step canvas (D8). stepTimelinePrimaries: the primaries D6 applies to (no Moments tab when the steps are the timeline). conceptPromotionDomains: whose flash cards may promote to a concept canvas. noFilmstripDomains: talking-head domains that get neither the auto-appended filmstrip nor a frame_strip attachment. sparseItemsMax / denseItemsMin: a tab at or below sparseItemsMax items takes one enriching attachment, one at or above denseItemsMin a "First up" header; the answer tab's "In short" header comes at any size. keyIdeasByDuration / keyIdeasCapFactor: content-model §9's key-ideas count by length (the band's low end: 5 / 8 / 12 / 16) and the factor the key-ideas cap takes over it (assemblerItemCapsNote).
measureUnitsNote: Words that make a label's leading number a measure, not a count ("7 Days in Tokyo", "10 Minute Abs", "3 Course Meal" — never rewritten to the shipped count, R3). One list for the summarizer (assembly/labels.py), the web (domain-meta.ts through @vie/shared/config) and the output-quality tools.
domainRequirementsNote: Per-domain assembled-output validation (_validate_domain_requirements in assembly/core.py): `required` components are backfilled from defaultTabs when the planner drops them (promotion equivalents count, e.g. comparison_radar satisfies comparison); `max` caps per-component tab counts; `forbidden` components are stripped at plan post-validation (before extraction burns tokens) AND again at assembly as a backstop — a forbidden component is never rendered for that domain regardless of what the planner emits. quiz_arena is allowed where the content is learnable (learning/language/tech/science, and a podcast or news explainer — output-quality D9; the quiz itself still needs is_learnable). Every domain must have an entry — an empty `required` is a deliberate decision (music: lyrics_karaoke optional so videos without per-line timing don't fail; podcast: moment_track segments are the spine; news: claims_tracker is the signature accountability surface; gaming: tier_list; sport: formation_diagram).
playbooksNote: Video-subtype layout playbooks keyed '<domain>:<format>' (format from the tier probe). Semantics: `forbidden` is a UNION with the domain's forbidden list; `required` OVERRIDES the domain's required list when present; `preferred` and `planGuidance` are rendered into the plan prompt's dynamic block so the LLM designs within the contract it will be held to. Enforcement lives in effective_requirements() (summarizer shared_config/domain_config.py) — consumed by plan post-validation and the assembly backstop.

gaming:unboxing.planGuidance: Box-opening / TCG pack-opening video: the pulls ARE the content. Rankings = the pulled cards (rarity or market-value bracket as tier, why it matters as reason). Highlights = the pull moments with timestamps. Never quiz the viewer on an unboxing.

review:unboxing.planGuidance: Product unboxing: lead with what was revealed and first impressions. Specs and contents as info_grid, reveal moments as moment_track. Never quiz the viewer on an unboxing.

learning:talk.planGuidance: Talk / keynote (content-model §1): open on Key ideas — spot_explorer on learning.keyIdeas (claim, why, quote, timestamp, kind), sectioned by the talk's parts; its figures ride as the numbers strip and its terms as a section of that tab, never an info_grid tab of their own. Then What they asked — checklist on learning.takeaways, only when the speaker makes 3+ explicit requests of the audience (an imperative said to the room, quotable) — never the speaker's own practices; Moments — moment_track on learning.timestamps, what each beat established. A concept_canvas only as a later tab when the concepts connect (the density table sets the minimum); claims_tracker on learning.claims only with has_claims, after the key ideas.

learning:lecture.planGuidance: Lecture (content-model §3): open on Concepts — concept_canvas on learning.concepts (definition, example, timestamp; it reads as a list first), the glossary inside it, never a second tab on the same source. Then Evidence & examples — spot_explorer on learning.keyIdeas (the experiments, studies and running examples, kind story / number); Moments — moment_track on learning.timestamps, what each section established; Test yourself last.

podcast:podcast.planGuidance: Podcast (content-model §2): open on Positions — spot_explorer on learning.keyIdeas (the claim, who holds it as speaker, why, the line, timestamp); stories (kind story) and the books / tools / people mentioned are sections of it, never their own info_grid tab. Then the Conversation map — moment_track on podcast.segments, what each segment concluded. No concept canvas unless the concepts connect (the density table sets the minimum); quotes ride on the positions.

podcast:interview.planGuidance: Interview (content-model §4; tags podcast + learning): open on Positions — spot_explorer on learning.keyIdeas, the guest's positions with speaker, disagreements as kind disagreement; the guests ride as its first section, never a tab of their own. Then Q&A — moment_track on podcast.qa, every substantive question, in the host's own words, with its answer; then the Conversation map — moment_track on podcast.segments; claims_tracker on podcast.claims only with has_claims, after the Q&A.

review:review.planGuidance: Product review (content-model §7): open on Pros & cons — comparison on review.pros, the pros and cons as the reviewer states them; the verdict rides in the hero, never in a tab. Then Features — spot_explorer on review.specs, the specs as its cells, never a standalone info_grid; vs competitors — comparison on review.comparisons (comparison_radar only when 4+ axes are numbers); Moments — the test scenes on learning.timestamps when learning is tagged.

news:explainer.planGuidance: News explainer (content-model §8): open on Claims — claims_tracker on news.claims (stated / supported / contested, the evidence, timestamp). Then Timeline — moment_track on news.storyTimeline, what happened at each step; Actors — spot_explorer on news.entities, the background context as its section, never an info_grid tab.

infoGridHostsNote: info_grid never stands alone (output-quality R6): the plan decides the fold — at plan-done (and again at frames-done) the reconcile pass (reconcile_pass.fold_step) moves a planned info_grid tab onto the planned tab that answers its question as one of its `folds` — the first tab whose component comes earliest in this list, a tab of the grid's own domain first among equals (assembly/info_grid_fold.fold_host). At assembly (apply_folds) a spot_explorer host takes the rows as cards in a section named after the grid; any other host takes the grid as a bottom attachment; a host that does not ship gives its folds back as tabs. No host → the grid stays a tab; a fold never leaves fewer than 3 planned tabs.
playbookAliasesNote: Probe formats that are another name for a playbook's format, per '<domain>:<format>' key (get_playbook in the summarizer's shared_config/domain_config.py reads a playbook's own key first, then its alias): a product review arrives as commentary or comparison, a news explainer as news, documentary or news_commentary (S07 commentary, S08 documentary), a podcast as commentary — also the probe's fallback for a label it does not know (keynote, fireside, conversation). learning:commentary has no alias on purpose: an explainer keeps keyPoints (D10), not the talk playbook. An interview the probe files under learning (a Talks at Google fireside, S14) arrives as learning:interview.
visualCriticalityNote: Adaptive frame-pipeline effort (derive_tier in media/visual_tier.py). HIGH: the visuals are the content (unboxings, travel, food) — over-select candidates and vision-describe them all so subject-matter frames win over presenter shots. LOW: talky formats where frames are decoration — skip vision. Everything else STANDARD. Derived from the tier probe (domain, format, has_visual_demo — derive_tier(probe, title)) which runs at transcript-ready; the frames branch waits for it at most 3 s before Step 6b, then falls back to the metadata rule (category/title keywords). highFormats: a probe format that alone makes a video HIGH. highTitleKeywords match as substrings ("pack opening" / "box opening" / "case opening" / "crate opening" and "booster" for a TCG opening titled "Opening … Booster Box!", never a bare "opening" — an opening keynote is a talk, output-quality 3.5). skipFormats (output-quality 3.5, D2, read only by skips_frames behind FRAMES_SKIP_WHEN_NO_VISUAL_DEMO): a video over 30 min whose probe (confidence above 0.6, the plan's bar) saw no visual demo and whose tier is not HIGH skips scene detection + vision when its tier is LOW or its probe format is listed here; [] = LOW only. Lectures stay off the list — their slides are content.

dataSourcesNote: Extraction field registry, one entry per path the planner may name as a tab dataSource (rendered into component_toolkit.txt's {valid_datasources} placeholder by render_valid_datasources() in the summarizer's shared_config/domain_config.py — entry order IS the prompt order). `field` is the key path inside the domain's extraction object (dotted for nested lists, e.g. tech.setup.commands). `kind`: list | object (an object counts as one item). `components`: components that can render the path (first = the defaultTab component when the path backs one). `siblings`: other paths sharing a component with this one, which can stand in when it is empty — assembly's sibling swap is component-based, so a sibling may differ in kind (fitness.exercises list ↔ fitness.timer object, both workout_room); every defaultTab sibling (sibling_datasources()) must be listed here. `requiresEvidence`: Appendix-C evidence key that must not be doubly-false for a tab on this path (null = never demoted); a has_code path doubly false at plan-done is decided at frames-done instead — code on screen keeps it). `waitsForVisual`: the field's content comes from the screen, so its extraction waits for frame annotations — gaming.highlights (on-screen pulls/plays) and the tech paths read off screen-shared code: tech.snippets, plus tech.patterns, tech.cheatSheet and tech.setup.commands, which quote the same on-screen code/terminal; transcript-driven paths (e.g. narrative.keyMoments) stay false. `cap`: max items asked for (largest SCALING bound in the domain schema, clamped to the primary component's assemblerItemCaps entry so extraction never asks for items the assembler truncates — e.g. language.phrases 25 (spot_explorer), language.vocabulary and podcast.quotes 15 (flash_deck); else the primary component's assemblerItemCaps/densityGates max; learning.timestamps = the assembler's duration-scaled moment_track max 60; learning.keyIdeas = 32, keyIdeasCapFactor × the longest keyIdeasByDuration band's count (assemblyPolicy) — the assembler caps a key-ideas tab by the video's length (assemblerItemCapsNote), not by spot_explorer's 25, and extraction stays complete up to that 2× ceiling (Kfir 2026-10-21; it was 20, which held the plan's expect below the ceiling); music.lyrics = 200 because lyrics_karaoke is uncapped and the schema asks for all lyrics). `outputWeight`: observed output tokens per item (whole object for kind=object), measured 2026-10-07 over the 31 stored v8 docs in the DEV Mongo (20 unique videos; read-only): mean cl100k tokens of each stored item (json.dumps) × a calibration factor of 1.488 (median of ledger tokens_out ÷ cl100k tokens of the stored extraction, over the 26 docs with exactly one Haiku extraction call) for extraction paths, and o200k × 1.144 (gpt-4o-mini; median over the 13 single-call docs whose quiz/flashcards/scenarios were all kept) for enrichment.quiz. 31 paths are observed (≥ 3 items); the other 30 (domains absent from dev: project, review, language, science, podcast, news, narrative; plus fitness.timer, gaming.loadout, gaming.walkthrough) use the schema skeleton item's cl100k size × the observed-vs-skeleton median ratio (2.025, over the 30 observed extraction paths) × 1.488. learning.keyIdeas (output-quality 1.1, the argued idea {claim, why, quote, timestamp, section, kind} of a talk, lecture or podcast — D10; keyPoints stays for explainers) is unobserved: learning.keyPoints' observed 141 × the two skeleton items' cl100k ratio (115 / 70) = 232; its components list stat_banner second — the answer tab's numbers strip reads its stamped figures (assembly/stat_banner.py); a secondary component is never planned. Output-quality 1.2 widened two observed items, rescaled by the same skeleton ratio: learning.timestamps gained `description` (required) + `quote` — 48 × 97 / 31 = 150 — and learning.concepts `timestamp` — 266 × 113 / 108 = 278. Output-quality 1.3 (podcast routing, L9/L11/L25/C10), by the skeleton method above: podcast.segments with a conclusion summary + `quote` 262; podcast.qa (new: an interview's {question, answer, speaker, timestamp, quote}, cap 15 — content-model §4's 8–15 exchanges; moment_track) 223; tech.topics as {name, description, timestamp} objects 108, spot_explorer first; podcast.quotes and narrative.quotes also render as spot_explorer quote cards (assembly/quote_spots.py). Output-quality 1.4 unfenced claims (D11, L10): learning.claims, podcast.claims and tech.claims carry news.claims' one shape {claim, source?, status: stated | supported | contested, sourceCitation?, timestamp} with its weight 187 and its has_claims gate — a talk, podcast or tech talk with has_claims may plan claims_tracker; none of them requires it, so requirementEvidence (which gates a required component) stays news-only. review.specs lists spot_explorer after its defaultTab's info_grid: the review playbook's Features tab shows the specs as cards (output-quality 1.6, R6). Output-quality 1.7 measured three learning paths on the S01 phase-1 iteration run (2026-10-21, 2 chunks, ledger outputTokens per group ÷ items): learning.keyIdeas 7,638 / 37 → 203, learning.timestamps 4,841 / 33 → 147, learning.takeaways 1,011 / 17 → 59. Initial values, tuned later.
demoteToNote: Demotion ladder used by reconcile at plan-done (pipeline-1min 3.2, summarizer pipeline/reconcile.py) when a tab's dataSource `requiresEvidence` key is doubly false (the plan AND the video memory answered false; a silent or failed reader is no opinion) and no same-component source in an active domain can take the tab: walk the list and take the first rung an ELIGIBLE dataSource renders — the source's declared siblings first, then the other paths of its own domain, in registry order. Eligible = an active domain, its own `requiresEvidence` not doubly false, and no other tab already reads it: the doubly-false source itself would render empty, and a source another tab shows would only duplicate that tab. No eligible rung (or an empty list) means drop the tab; a moment_track tab is kept instead, for assembly's moment fallback chain. Independent of the assembly-time _DEMOTE_LADDER (assembly/promotion.py), which reacts to assembler failures after extraction. Entries beyond the brief's six mirror that ladder minus display_section, so every component of an evidence-gated dataSource has an entry.
requirementEvidenceNote: Evidence key gating each domain's `required` component (domainRequirements): reconcile at plan-done (pipeline-1min 3.2) appends the domain's defaultTab for a missing required component unless this key is doubly false (the plan AND the video memory answered false; a silent or failed reader is no opinion), and assembly's backfill applies the same rule as the backstop. A key the screen can still answer (has_code — tech's code_playground) is not ruled out at plan-done when doubly false: the backfill is deferred to frames-done (deferred_to_frames), where code on screen adds the defaultTab (a fresh meta follows) and no code on screen records it not_backfilled. Domain required components not listed here (language/science spot_explorer, podcast moment_track) stay unconditional. This map gates a requirement; whether a tab may read a path at all is the path's own dataSources[*].requiresEvidence — e.g. has_code on all four tech code paths (snippets, patterns, cheatSheet, setup.commands; Kfir's gate-2 decision 7: a non-code talk gets no empty code tab).
quizPolicyNote: Quiz placement, gating and size (output-quality D9, R12; D9 revised 2026-10-23): the quiz is the LAST tab (reconcile at plan-done and the assembly backstop move it there), needs is_learnable not doubly false and ships only on the instructional `formats` — tier-probe format ids (prompts/tier_probe.txt, probe_types.VALID_FORMATS): `lecture` (a class, a course session, an explainer that builds up concepts) and `tutorial` (a how-to the viewer follows), never a talk, interview, podcast, news or any other format; a planned quiz on another format is dropped at reconcile (droppedTabs `reconcile_quiz_format`) and no quiz call is made (quiz_format.quiz_format_allowed; an unknown format — no probe answer, a category override — rules nothing out). It is untimed (`timer` — the web registry passes it to QuizArena's withTimer) and gets `questionsByDuration`: the first band whose `maxMinutes` the video's length does not exceed (null = no upper bound) sets the count the quiz prompt asks for (enrichment.quiz_question_count; an unknown length is sized as the middle band, memory.UNKNOWN_LENGTH_SECONDS), never above enrichment.quiz's registry cap. Bands = content-model §9: ≤ 15 min → 3, ≤ 45 min → 5, longer → 8. attachmentHostsExclude: components that never host the quick_quiz strip.
quizEnrichmentNote: Quiz-only enrichment (pipeline-1min phase 1d): the quiz call runs only for these domains (the ones whose domainRequirements do not forbid quiz_arena); `flavor` is the per-domain role line of enrich_quiz.txt, carried over from the per-domain enrich prompts it replaced in phase 1d. The call is demand-driven: it runs only when the plan has a quiz_arena tab or a tab that can host a quick_quiz (needs_quiz() in the summarizer's services/pipeline/enrichment.py).

flavor.learning: Test the speaker's claims and the reasoning behind them — what is argued, why, and the figures it turns on — never a detail for its own sake.
flavor.language: Test comprehension of vocabulary, grammar rules, and usage — practical language skills the viewer can use immediately.
flavor.tech: Think like a senior developer onboarding a teammate — test understanding of technical decisions, code patterns, and commands from the video.
flavor.science: Test understanding of scientific concepts, facts, and relationships — and their real-world applications.
flavor.podcast: Test understanding of the positions argued in the conversation — who claims what and why — never trivia about the hosts or the show.
flavor.news: Test understanding of what happened, who is involved and what the evidence says — never a date or a name asked for its own sake.

groupingNote: Phase-3 extraction grouping: at most maxTextGroups text groups (+ 1 visual group for waitsForVisual paths); a domain splits by field when Σ outputWeight × expected items exceeds groupOutputBudget output tokens, and a slice estimated under minGroupOutput tokens joins the domain's previous slice instead of costing a call of its own (output-quality 1.7, L16: S01's 17 asks — ~300 tokens — were a third call per chunk for a 4-second answer; every call re-reads the cached transcript).
